mechanism: Subretinal lentiviral Equine Infectious Anemia Virus vector gene therapy expressing the anti-angiogenic proteins endostatin and angiostatin for neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
phase: Phase 1 long-term safety follow-up; prior Phase 1 GEM dose-escalation treatment study completed
development_status: Inactive/discontinued commercial development. ClinicalTrials.gov lists NCT01678872 as active, not recruiting for long-term safety follow-up of prior RetinoStat recipients through estimated March 2029, but Oxford BioMedica/OXB discontinued work on OXB-201 after an internal pipeline review and moved wet AMD work to OXB-203.
clinical_summary: NCT01678872 is not a new efficacy-enabling treatment trial; it follows patients who previously received RetinoStat in protocol RS1/001/10. The prior GEM Phase 1 study enrolled 21 advanced neovascular AMD patients and showed dose-related, durable intraocular expression of endostatin and angiostatin, but clinical activity was limited: the peer-reviewed report found only one subject with convincing anti-permeability activity in a late-stage population and no significant mean lesion-size change at the highest tested dose. Any potential differentiation is therefore historical proof-of-concept for ocular lentiviral delivery rather than an active launch thesis.
safety_summary: The prior GEM Phase 1 report stated that all tested doses were well tolerated, with no dose-limiting toxicities, little or no ocular inflammation, and one procedure-related serious adverse event, a macular hole that resolved after management. Oxford BioMedica reported no serious adverse events related to the product in the Phase 1 publication announcement. NCT01678872 continues adverse-event and BCVA follow-up over 14 years, but ClinicalTrials.gov has no posted results.
management_tools: Exclude from near-term launch readiness, formulary build, and budget-impact forecasting unless OXB-201 is publicly reactivated.
Keep as a historical long-term safety follow-up item; monitor ClinicalTrials.gov for status changes or posted long-term results.
If reactivated, reassess as a one-time ocular gene therapy under medical-benefit gene-therapy governance with retinal-specialist administration criteria.
evidence_gaps: ClinicalTrials.gov has no posted results for NCT01678872 despite the follow-up study remaining active, not recruiting.
No current Oxford BioMedica/OXB source was found showing active RetinoStat/OXB-201 development, regulatory filing plans, or commercial launch intent.
Annual cost is set to $0 because the asset is discontinued/inactive with no expected commercialization; no RetinoStat price exists.
Clinical efficacy evidence is limited by the small, open-label Phase 1 study in advanced late-stage neovascular AMD and lack of a controlled efficacy trial.
NCT01678872 is a follow-up study of prior RetinoStat recipients, not a study recruiting or dosing new patients.

sources.title: A Long Term Follow-up Study to Evaluate the Safety of RetinoStat in Patients With Age-Related Macular Degeneration
supports: Official title is a long-term follow-up study to evaluate safety of RetinoStat in age-related macular degeneration.
Sponsor is Oxford BioMedica; study identifier is RS1/002/11.
Overall status is active, not recruiting; status was verified January 2026; last update posted was 2026-01-14.
Estimated enrollment is 18; start date was August 2012; estimated primary completion and completion are March 2029.
Intervention is RetinoStat for long-term follow-up of patients who received RetinoStat in a previous study.
Primary outcome is incidence of adverse events over 14 years; secondary outcome is change from baseline in best-corrected visual acuity over 14 years.
Eligibility requires prior subretinal RetinoStat injection and enrollment in protocol RS1/001/10.
ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults is false.

sources.title: A Phase I Dose Escalation Safety Study of Subretinally Injected RetinoStat, a Lentiviral Vector Expressing Endostatin and Angiostatin, in Patients With Advanced Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration
supports: Prior GEM study protocol RS1/001/10 evaluated subretinally injected RetinoStat in advanced neovascular AMD.
RetinoStat was described as a lentiviral vector expressing endostatin and angiostatin.
Overall status is completed; actual enrollment was 21; actual primary completion was September 2014 and actual completion was May 2015.
Design was single-group, open-label Phase 1 with escalating single subretinal injections and a dose-confirmation phase.
Primary outcome was incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events through 24 weeks.
ClinicalTrials.gov links the peer-reviewed result publication by Campochiaro et al. in Human Gene Therapy.

sources.title: Lentiviral Vector Gene Transfer of Endostatin/Angiostatin for Macular Degeneration (GEM) Study
supports: RetinoStat is an EIAV lentiviral vector expressing endostatin and angiostatin.
Patients with advanced neovascular AMD received subretinal RetinoStat doses of 2.4 x 10^4, 2.4 x 10^5, or 8.0 x 10^5 transduction units.
All doses were well tolerated with no dose-limiting toxicities and little or no ocular inflammation.
One procedure-related serious adverse event, a macular hole, was managed and resolved.
Endostatin and angiostatin expression showed a vector dose-related increase and remained stable through week 48, with longer-term expression maintained at last measurement in available subjects.
Only one subject showed convincing evidence of anti-permeability activity, and there was no significant mean lesion-size change in subjects injected with 8.0 x 10^5 transduction units.

sources.title: Publication of RetinoStat (OXB-201) Phase I study
supports: Oxford BioMedica announced publication of RetinoStat/OXB-201 Phase 1 data in Human Gene Therapy.
The company stated the Phase 1 study met its primary endpoint of safety and tolerability.
The company stated RetinoStat showed favorable safety and sustained expression of endostatin and angiostatin in the eye.
The company stated no serious adverse events related to the product had been observed to date.
At that time, Oxford BioMedica said it was evaluating the optimal way to progress clinical development.

sources.title: Oxford BioMedica provides update on RetinoStat Programme
supports: Oxford BioMedica announced it would regain worldwide rights to RetinoStat for wet AMD.
Sanofi notified Oxford BioMedica it would not continue development beyond the ongoing Phase 1 study due to pipeline prioritization.
Oxford BioMedica stated Sanofi's decision was not linked to unexpected results based on study data analyzed to date.
The company described RetinoStat as potentially requiring only a single administration if confirmed.

sources.title: Oxford Biomedica Annual report and accounts 2019
supports: Oxford BioMedica's 2019 annual report product pipeline listed OXB-203 in wet AMD as preclinical rather than RetinoStat/OXB-201.
The report described OXB-203 as targeting wet AMD by expressing aflibercept and noted prior OXB-201 used endostatin and angiostatin.
The report supports that the company's wet AMD development focus had shifted away from OXB-201/RetinoStat.

sources.title: Oxford Biomedica: Juno deal expands CAR-T revenue streams
supports: Edison reported that Oxford BioMedica completed an internal pipeline review and discontinued work on OXB-201 for wet AMD.
Edison reported that OXB-203 took over from predecessor OXB-201 for wet AMD.
This source corroborates the inactive/discontinued interpretation, but the annual report is prioritized as the company source for the current pipeline shift.

sources.title: Oxford Biomedica rebrands as OXB reinforcing transformation into leading global cell and gene therapy CDMO
supports: Oxford BioMedica stated it was rebranding as OXB and transforming into a global pure-play cell and gene therapy CDMO.
The company described its mission as enabling clients to deliver cell and gene therapies through CDMO services.
Current company positioning supports low near-term commercial disruption from historical proprietary RetinoStat development.

expected_launch_window.method: Combined NCT01678872's long-term follow-up-only design with evidence that OXB-201/RetinoStat was discontinued and replaced by OXB-203 in OXB's wet AMD pipeline.
expected_launch_window.explanation: The CT.gov study remains active only to monitor prior recipients; there is no public evidence of active RetinoStat development, filing, or commercialization.

annual_cost_range.method: Assigned $0 because the asset is discontinued/inactive with no expected launch; no analog price was applied because there is no active commercial scenario to price.
annual_cost_range.explanation: A one-time ocular gene-therapy analog would only be relevant if OXB-201 were reactivated; current payer budget exposure is nil.

clinical_differentiation.method: Weighted durable ocular transgene expression and favorable early safety against limited demonstrated clinical activity, Phase 1-only evidence, and discontinued development.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: RetinoStat was scientifically differentiated as an early ocular lentiviral gene-therapy proof of concept, but the evidence does not support meaningful active pipeline differentiation for payer launch planning.

budget_impact.method: Rated from inactive/discontinued status, absence of launch timing, and follow-up-only CT.gov design.
budget_impact.explanation: No treated population growth, pricing, or utilization controls are expected unless the asset is publicly reactivated.

disruption_risk.method: Rated from the absence of active commercial development and the fact that NCT01678872 only monitors prior recipients.
disruption_risk.explanation: Operational work is limited to periodic monitoring of trial status and posted long-term safety results.

recommended_action.method: Recommended routine monitoring because the program is inactive but the long-term safety follow-up study remains active, not recruiting.
recommended_action.explanation: No formulary build or active planning is warranted unless OXB-201 development is restarted or new long-term results materially change the evidence base.

quality_flags: Discontinued/inactive asset: Oxford BioMedica/OXB-201 RetinoStat should not be treated as an upcoming launch based solely on NCT01678872's active-not-recruiting follow-up status.
Follow-up-only trial: NCT01678872 enrolls patients who already received RetinoStat under protocol RS1/001/10 and is intended to monitor long-term safety, not dose new patients.
No posted ClinicalTrials.gov results for NCT01678872.
Prior treatment evidence is Phase 1, open-label, small-sample, and not a controlled efficacy dataset.
Annual cost is intentionally $0 because there is no expected commercialization; this should be revisited only if public evidence shows program reactivation.
